tour.title: Welcome & Developer Conventions
tour.description: Start with CLAUDE.md to understand the monorepo workspace configuration, standard development commands, and production deployment assumptions. This file details the target architecture running on Hostinger and the monorepo structure containing the main apps/web application.
tour.languageLesson: The CLAUDE.md file outlines CLI commands using pnpm workspaces. Since there is no linter or test suite configured in this repository, TypeScript type-checking serves as the primary code correctness validator.

tour.title: Database Schemas & Models
tour.description: Examine the PostgreSQL tables, enums, and relations managed via Drizzle ORM. Drizzle is lazily initialized to prevent database client creation at module import time, preventing serverless cold-start bottlenecks.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle ORM defines tables using TypeScript schemas (e.g., pgTable, pgEnum). By wrapping the database instantiation in a lazy-loading proxy wrapper or function, the app avoids opening unnecessary sockets during serverless initialization.

tour.title: Global Data Access Queries
tour.description: Inspect the single most interconnected module in the application, queries.ts, which defines all global database read/write queries. It manages orders, school catalogs, tenant custom settings, active children sessions, and platform reports.
tour.languageLesson: Drizzle transactions use the db.transaction() method to chain multiple operations atomically. In queries.ts, updating workflow configurations and registering settings logs are executed inside a single transaction to guarantee data integrity.

tour.title: Multi-Tenant Routing & Layout
tour.description: Trace the entry flow for parent users, starting from the home school selector page and transitioning into dynamic tenant layout frames. The layout component dynamically loads metadata and tenant accent colors based on the sub-path slug.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router dynamic routing represents tenant subdomains or slugs as directory folders (e.g., [tenant]). Layout files in Next.js execute server-side data fetching and propagate children nodes, serving as wrappers that inject theme styling context.

tour.title: The School Storefront & Catalog Grid
tour.description: Explore the public shopping catalog grid and product detail configurations tailored for parent uniform selection. Garments are rendered dynamically using scalable vector graphics (SVG) based on garment IDs rather than loading image assets.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js client components utilize the 'use client' directive to declare interactive state nodes. Sizing filters and search queries dynamically update state parameters to filter uniform displays in real-time.

tour.title: Sizing Control & Cart Persistence
tour.description: Learn how parents customize garment orders by choosing color and size variants and adding them to the cart. Shopping carts are stored locally in the parent's browser using localStorage, persisting item details across storefront sub-pages.
tour.languageLesson: Local storage access in React requires handling hydration mismatches. The cart-store uses custom React hooks (such as useEffect) to defer reading from localStorage key 'uo:cart:v1' until the component has mounted on the client.

tour.title: Checkout & Stripe Destination Charges
tour.description: Examine the checkout screen and the API endpoint producing Stripe Payment Intents. Payments leverage Stripe Connect standard accounts to routes funds directly to the target school tenant while managing application fees.
tour.languageLesson: Stripe Connect destination charges specify an application_fee_amount and transfer_data destination. This routes the parent's payment directly to the school's account while capturing the commission on the platform master account.

tour.title: Securing Webhook Events & Recording Orders
tour.description: Walk through the Stripe webhook receiver that processes transaction success, refunds, and account updates, alongside the orders endpoint. Secure webhooks ensure that order records are logged in Drizzle only after payment is verified.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js API route handlers process POST payloads using standard Request objects. To verify signatures, webhooks parse raw request buffers using stripe.webhooks.constructEvent() to prevent spoofing attacks.

tour.title: Fulfillment Notifications & Email Templates
tour.description: Examine the transactional notification system that informs parent shoppers when order states change. It uses EmailIt client APIs to dispatch customized HTML mailers for confirmations, ready-for-pickup notifications, holds, or refunds.
tour.languageLesson: Email templates are compiled using React components (via @react-email or similar) and serialized to raw HTML strings. The dispatch engine integrates these templates to generate standardized, responsive structures.

tour.title: Order Operations & Admin Kanban Boards
tour.description: Explore the administrative order-handling portal where school operators track active orders through a custom Kanban board interface. Operators can filter status columns, resolve customer issues, print pick slips, and trigger fulfillment actions.
tour.languageLesson: React-based boards structure columns by mapping arrays of statuses. By rendering conditional action triggers (such as marking orders as ready or completed), the client updates states by invoking server actions.

tour.title: Platform Tenant Onboarding Wizard
tour.description: Trace the multi-step tenant-creation workflow designed for platform administrators. The superadmin wizard creates draft subdomains, configures accent colors, connects Stripe payouts, clones catalogs from templates, and publishes tenant systems.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-step client wizards manage wizard states as sequential steps. In actions.ts, catalog items are duplicated by performing insert-select transactions that copy items from global templates to the new tenant's schema space.

tour.title: Continuous Integration Type Safety Check
tour.description: Investigate the continuous integration workflow running on GitHub Actions. It runs the type correctness check across all workspaces, acting as the final pipeline gate before deployment.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions pipeline YAML configurations define triggers and jobs. This workflow runs pnpm check-types across packages to catch TypeScript compile-time violations before deployment.
